source_documents.title: The Dark State, Vibronic Coupling, and Viscosity Sensing of Methoxylated Benzoyl Coumarins

reference_evidence_units.quote: However, the observed fluorescence quenching is better ascribed to the presence of a dark charge transfer (1CT) state.
reference_evidence_units.subject: BC8, BC6
reference_evidence_units.statement: Quenching comes from a dark CT state, not from TICT.

reference_evidence_units.quote: These computational analyses confirmed the presence of a dark CT (1CT) state with a small energy gap to emissive hybridized local and charge-transfer (1HLCT) state by both TD-DFT and ADC(2) methods.
reference_evidence_units.subject: BC8, BC6
reference_evidence_units.statement: Dark 1CT lies close to the emissive 1HLCT state.

reference_evidence_units.quote: Under high-viscosity conditions, the restriction of 1HLCT ! 1CT transition and configurational conversion effectively suppresses nonradiative decay, thereby leading to enhanced FL emission.
reference_evidence_units.subject: BC8, BC6
reference_evidence_units.statement: Viscosity blocks the HLCT-to-CT conversion and turns emission on.

reference_evidence_units.quote: The oscillator strengths of AC8 and BC8 (≈0.03) are smaller than those of BC6 and AC6 (0.12–0.13), which agrees with the lower FL emission QY of 8-methoxyl coumarins as compared to 6-methoxyl coumarins in ACN.
reference_evidence_units.subject: BC8 vs BC6
reference_evidence_units.statement: The 8-methoxy isomers have a weaker S1 transition and lower QY.

reference_evidence_units.quote: The computed FL QY for the studied compounds is found to range from 14.5 to 16.7% (Table 4), corroborating the observed
reference_evidence_units.subject: AC/BC series
reference_evidence_units.statement: Computed kfl/kIC reproduce the low-temperature QY.

reference_evidence_units.quote: To date, the mechanism of viscosity sensing has predominantly been attributed to a twisted intramolecular charge transfer effect.
reference_evidence_units.subject: viscosity probes
reference_evidence_units.statement: The paper sets its dark-CT account against the usual TICT account.

reference_evidence_units.quote: The 6-methoxyl coumarin contains heightened emission as compared to its 8-methoxyl counterparts in solvents.
reference_evidence_units.subject: 6- vs 8-methoxy
reference_evidence_units.statement: e.g. BC8 0.29% vs higher QY for the 6-isomers in ACN (Table 1).

reference_mechanisms.label: RIM_RIR_RIV
reference_mechanisms.rationale: Viscosity restricts the HLCT-to-CT configurational conversion.

reference_mechanisms.label: ICT_TICT_CT
reference_mechanisms.rationale: The quenching state is a (non-twisted) dark CT state and the emitter is an HLCT state; the paper argues against TICT.

reference_mechanisms.label: RADIATIVE_RATE_STATE_BALANCE
reference_mechanisms.rationale: Emission is controlled by a dark 1CT state close to the emissive 1HLCT state; oscillator strength and computed kfl/kIC explain the QY differences.

contrast_group.varied_factor: methoxy position on the 3-benzoyl coumarin (8 vs 6)
contrast_group.paper_difference: The 8-methoxy isomer has a weak S1 transition (f about 0.03 vs 0.12) and lower QY; both are viscosity-sensitive through the dark 1CT state.
